description_full: Nagase & Co., Ltd. manufactures, imports/exports, and sells chemicals, plastics, electronic materials, cosmetics, and health foods worldwide. It offers resin raw materials, monomers, resins, solvents, pigments, dyes, dispersing materials, additives, urethane raw materials, flame retardants, release agents, conductive materials, functional sheets, films, adhesives, and sanitary materials. The company also provides petrochemical products, metal processing oil, surfactants and related raw materials, environmental equipment and chemicals, electronic chemicals, UV-curing agent materials, and chemical outsourcing coordination services. In addition, it offers engineering, general-purpose, packaging, and other plastic-related products and services; precision abrasive materials, optical materials, touch-panel components, functional paints, conductive and insulating materials, adhesive and sealing materials, heat-resistant films, optical lenses, chemical management devices, low dielectric materials, LED lighting, sensing devices, IoT modules, optical materials for XR, and semiconductor- and electronic device-related equipment. Further, the company provides modified epoxy resins and related products, photolithography materials for flat panel displays and semiconductors, and materials related to 3D printing; mobility interior and exterior functional parts, including various resins, functional paints, adhesives, lightweight parts, decorative parts, and HMI parts; xEV-related parts, thermal control parts, battery materials, sensors, LiDAR-related parts, and autonomous driving technologies. Additionally, it offers pharmaceuticals, in vitro diagnostics, raw materials for cosmetics and household products, food materials, premixes, agricultural, fisheries, and livestock-related materials, and endotoxin removal services. The company was founded in 1832 and is headquartered in Osaka, Japan.

financial_summary: Nagase & Co., Ltd. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $3.0B market cap on $6.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $123M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.44× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.2× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 6.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

Commodity price volatility and cost-curve position — in a downturn only the lowest-cost producer has a business, and the rest carry the overhead.
Environmental remediation liability — tightening regulations on emissions, tailings, and water use create open-ended balance-sheet risk that grows with each legislative cycle.
Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.
